junction.name: Whitestone Expressway & Linden Place, New York City

claims.text: Whitestone Expressway & Linden Place had 60 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 3 pedestrians injured, 0 cyclists injured and 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $4.1 million a year.
48% of crashes here had only people in vehicles hurt, against 24% at the city's priority junctions.
19% of crashes here had “following too closely” recorded as a contributing factor, against 6% at the city's priority junctions.
9% of crashes here had “unsafe lane changing” recorded as a contributing factor, against 2% at the city's priority junctions.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: worked (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +8%) could be zero).
Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 3.3 crashes a year (CMF 4215, the median of 4 eligible records), worth $1.1 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.8 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites), worth $616,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 is responsible for I 678 (owner recorded in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory).
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Whitestone Expressway, Linden Place (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 19, New York City Council; Queens Community Board 7.
A request letter to the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 and the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
